answer: An agent economy can make reputation costly to counterfeit by requiring each new identity to lock a scarce token in a public bond, then slash that bond if the identity is caught double-voting or laundering rewards through linked accounts. Honest agents can use the bond as a haven for disputes, while a trellis of repeated interactions helps expose coordinated identities; at the nadir, a Sybil attacker must risk real capital for every persona and wait for each one to build trust.
